name: modal
title: Modal
description: The confirmation of something that cannot be undone: quit, sign out, delete, leave a live round. Never for information and never for a reward; those are a toast, a sheet or feedback. It always carries exactly two actions, a destructive one first on the negative colour carrying `data-gs-destructive`, and a safe one raised under it, and it refuses to render without the destructive one, which its unit test holds it to. Centred in its container over a heavier scrim than the sheet's. A tap on the scrim does nothing and Escape is the safe action, so nobody quits by reaching for the scene behind the question. Focus lands on the safe action, is held inside while open, and goes back to what had it. `data-gs-tone` is `warning` for leaving something behind and `negative` for destroying something; the glyph disc takes the colour. Performs nothing: it does not quit, sign out or delete anything.
docs: Put `position: relative` on the surface the modal belongs to and render it inside. Pass `open`, a `title` that is the question ("Quit this game?"), `destructiveAction` and `safeAction`, each a label and a handler. The host owns `open` and closes the modal from either handler; the modal closes nothing itself. Pass `tone="negative"` when the action destroys something rather than leaves it. Put what it costs in `children`, one sentence. Do not reach for it to tell the player something: that is a toast. Do not reach for it to show a reward: that is a sheet. It depends on `sheet` for the focus trap the two share.
